newsitem.title: UK: Experts warn on safety at Lithuanian nuclear plant.
newsitem.headline: Experts warn on safety at Lithuanian nuclear plant.

text.p: Experts have warned Lithuania not to restart its Ignalina nuclear power plant after it is closed this year for maintenance unless new safety measures have been taken, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development said on Friday.
The bank said in a statement that important failings in the design and operation of the power station's two units must be sorted out before they are put back in operation.
Ignalina, home to the two largest Chernobyl-style reactors in the former Soviet Union, has been the scene of a number of accidents in recent years.
It is slated for closure in 2010, when its reactor channels will need to be replaced.

The safety assessors, commissioned by the bank and the Lithuanian government, were asked to decide whether or not the units could be operated safely during the time before the fuel channels needed replacing.

"Under the Nuclear Safety Account grant agreement, the Lithuanian government has undertaken the commitment not to extend the lifetime of either unit beyond the time at which its fuel channels should be replaced," the bank said.
The independent panel of experts carried out an in-depth assessment of the Ignalina plant last year.
